definitions.explanation: A handheld optical instrument with two lenses for viewing distant objects, used for birdwatching, sports events, concerts, and stargazing.

examples.japanese: {双眼鏡|そうがんきょう}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{鳥|とり}→鳥：00679_tori⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{観察|かんさつ}する→観察する：21989_kansatsusuru⟧。
⟦コンサート→コンサート：01360_konsaato⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{双眼鏡|そうがんきょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{持|も}って→持つ：00478_motsu⟧いった。
examples.english: I brought binoculars to the concert.

examples.japanese: {双眼鏡|そうがんきょう}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{覗|のぞ}く→覗く：02388_nozoku⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、{遠|とお}く⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{山|やま}→山：02168_yama⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{頂上|ちょうじょう}→頂上：03493_choujou⟧⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧⟦{見|み}えた→見える：01165_mieru⟧。
examples.english: When I looked through the binoculars, I could see all the way to the distant mountain peak.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {双眼鏡|そうがんきょう}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{見|み}る→見る：00283_miru⟧ (look through binoculars)
- {双眼鏡|そうがんきょう}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{覗|のぞ}く→覗く：02388_nozoku⟧ (peer through binoculars)
- {双眼鏡|そうがんきょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{構|かま}える→構える：09567_kamaeru⟧ (raise binoculars to one's eyes)

USAGE:
The word is composed of {双|そう} (pair), {眼|がん} (eye), and {鏡|きょう} (lens/mirror). For a single-lens telescope, use ⟦{望遠鏡|ぼうえんきょう}→望遠鏡：05483_bouenkyou⟧. In Japan, compact {双眼鏡|そうがんきょう} are especially popular at concerts and theater performances where seats may be far from the stage. Small opera-glass-type binoculars are also called {双眼鏡|そうがんきょう}.
